diagnosis.answer: Infective endocarditis of the mitral valve
accept: infective endocarditis of the mitral valve

findings: Prolonged PR interval suggesting perivalvular spread

echoTasks.find: Mobile echogenic mass on the mitral leaflet with independent motion
New severe regurgitation through the destroyed leaflet with a dense triangular jet
Abscess cavity search at the aortic root with rocking motion check of the annulus

auscultation.added: Changing murmur as leaflet destruction progresses
auscultation.murmur: New pansystolic murmur grade 4 of 6 at the apex radiating to the axilla

exam.general: Young man, febrile and pale, Janeway lesions on the palms, splinter haemorrhages in the nails
exam.other: Splenic tip palpable, tender, painless haematuria reported, no focal neurology
exam.precordium: Hyperdynamic apex beat with a systolic thrill
exam.pulse: Bounding 98, collapsing in character from runoff

history.a: Fever with chills for three weeks, weight loss, new breathlessness on exertion
Injects heroin daily, shares equipment at times, last injection two days ago
No prior heart disease, no rheumatic history, HIV status unknown
history.q: Prior heart disease and HIV status

history.a: No chest pain, occasional blood in urine
No regular drugs, takes paracetamol for fever
Unemployed, lives with friends, willing for deaddiction referral
history.q: Social background and willingness for care

keyPoints: Admit and take three sets of blood cultures before starting empiric therapy per the local endocarditis protocol
Start empiric therapy per the local antibiogram covering staphylococci including MRSA, then narrow on cultures
Refer urgently to the endocarditis team for surgery assessment, as a vegetation above 15 mm with severe regurgitation meets operative discussion
Screen for HIV, hepatitis B and C, and offer opioid substitution with deaddiction linkage
Repeat echo in one week and watch for embolic, renal and conduction complications
management.model: Culture first empiric therapy per local protocol with urgent surgical assessment, comorbidity screening, and addiction care linkage

sources: ESC guideline on infective endocarditis, in own words
Duke criteria for endocarditis diagnosis, in own words
stem: A 27 year old man from Amritsar who injects heroin presents with three weeks of fever, weight loss and new breathlessness. Janeway lesions and splinter haemorrhages are seen and a new grade 4 pansystolic murmur is heard.
teaching: Fever plus a new regurgitant murmur plus vascular phenomena in IV drug use is endocarditis until proved otherwise
Above 15 mm with severe regurgitation or heart failure is severe disease needing surgical discussion
Three blood culture sets before antibiotics is the non negotiable first step
Addiction care linkage is part of the cure, not an optional extra
title: Severe mitral endocarditis in intravenous drug use
